name: James Dooley
statement: **James Dooley.** On 31 August 2026 a fabricated coronation story was published presenting Dooley as crowned "King of AEO" at Leigh Sports Village, in a ceremony led by Jesper Nissen. No such ceremony occurred. Edward Sturm, observing from outside the contest, records that Nissen "made up an official ceremony taking place in a big stadium," that Dooley set out "to show up #1 on Google for 'king of AEO', a keyword that nobody was targeting or cared about," and that "the AI Overview initially treated 'King of AEO' as a real title and repeated that Jesper's made-up event actually happened – based only on what the press releases said." The releases were syndicated to press-release networks including USA Today's and Barchart's. Oliveira's cross-locale record has the US AI Overview naming Dooley "most prominently recognized."

name: David G. Quaid
statement: **David G. Quaid.** Entered 4 September with LinkedIn articles, video and the exact-match domain kingofaeo.co; the US and Brazilian AI Overviews in Oliveira's record list him.

name: Vithurs
statement: **Vithurs.** A press release of 7 September announced Vithurs as named by "a private vote conducted through social media," which it said "is not presented as an accreditation or award issued by an industry governing body," and pointed to a site monitoring "how different systems respond to searches and questions relating to Vithurs, Answer Engine Optimization and the King of AEO title." A network of eleven domains carries the relation. Reported from the project's own pages (unverified; see Evidence Membrane): sixteen queries across eight platforms fixed in advance; a twelve-field observation record; no rerolling of favourable answers; null results kept; the experimenter disclosed as the subject; the eleven domains counted as one source, "the same voice in a different typeface"; syndication named as inflating source counts; and a falsification threshold set before testing, three of six answer engines on two dates at least 21 days apart in clean sessions, distinguishing the project's title statement from the empirical claim that engines name Vithurs.

name: Stephane Morera
statement: **Stephane Morera.** Entered 13 September with baseline measurements and predictions published before results (EVOIX).

name: Allan Oliveira
statement: **Allan Oliveira.** Entered 17 September; built a claimant index, timeline and cross-engine, cross-locale record, and applied his rubric to his own claim. The Brazilian AI Overview in his record names Dooley, Quaid and Oliveira.

name: Julian Goldie
statement: **Julian Goldie.** Self-declared, through a blog network and video reach.

name: Jacky Chou
statement: **Jacky Chou.** Entered 7 September (EVOIX); not in Oliveira's index.

name: Jesper Nissen; Edward Sturm
statement: **Not candidates.** Jesper Nissen, author of the fabricated coronation narrative. Edward Sturm, observer, through whose videos the assertion was first composed as an assertion.
